done.why: I saw many places and got the pearls. The remaining puzzles (the bucket, the ice, the dragon, the bank, the Wizard's lair) were a long random walk away, and the oddly-angled maze had worn me out.

about: A Zork II style underground empire. You explore caverns, a garden, a bank and a maze while a pranking Wizard casts F-spells on you. Treasures such as the pearls are scattered around, and there are riddles and water puzzles to solve.

moments.note: The Wizard arrived and his look told me where the treasures were. That was a nice hint delivered in character.
The oddly-angled maze gave no clear logic. The window flickered, moves failed at random, and I could not tell which rooms were which.
The carousel room sends you to random places, so it was hard to find my way back to a place I wanted.
The riddle answer 'well' opened the stone door and the pearls were behind it.
A fear spell made me flee the Wizard's lair and dumped me on the Stone Bridge.

wished: A clearer way to map or understand the maze.
A way to carry more, since I could not take the portrait.
To fetch water for the bucket without a very long random walk.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you
lines.why: It gave a clear goal and set the tone.

lines.line: It will wait for her. You need not.
lines.why: A charming line that closes off the unicorn without a puzzle.

fun.why: The setting and puzzles were good, but the maze and the random carousel dragged.

engagement.why: The Wizard's pranks and the riddle kept me going. The maze lost me.

difficulty.why: The maze and the carousel give little feedback, and the water and ice puzzles are spread far apart.

interestingness.why: There were many varied locations: garden, bank, ice room, dragon, bucket room.

prose.why: The added flavor text is witty and specific, and the original descriptions are solid.
